hints.title: Two Paths to Interview Qualification
hints.text: A user qualifies if they won gold in at least three competitions or medaled in three or more consecutive contests.

hints.title: Consecutive Medal Streak Detection
hints.text: Unpivot all medal winners (gold, silver, bronze) with contest_id, compute row_number ordered by contest_id, and group by (contest_id - row_number) having count >= 3.

hints.title: Combining Candidate Streams
hints.text: Union candidates from gold medal counts with candidates from consecutive medal streaks, then join Users for names and emails.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AllMedals AS (
    SELECT contest_id, gold_medal AS user_id FROM Contests
    UNION ALL
    SELECT contest_id, silver_medal AS user_id FROM Contests
    UNION ALL
    SELECT contest_id, bronze_medal AS user_id FROM Contests
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT
        user_id,
        contest_id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY contest_id) AS grp
    FROM AllMedals
),
ConsecutiveWinners AS (
    SELECT user_id
    FROM Streaks
    GROUP BY user_id, grp
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
),
GoldWinners AS (
    SELECT gold_medal AS user_id
    FROM Contests
    GROUP BY gold_medal
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
),
CandidateIds AS (
    SELECT user_id FROM ConsecutiveWinners
    UNION
    SELECT user_id FROM GoldWinners
)
SELECT u.name, u.mail
FROM Users u
JOIN CandidateIds c ON u.user_id = c.user_id;
```

complexity.time: O(C log C) window sort over medal records
complexity.notes: Gaps-and-islands streak detection combined with frequency aggregation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self-joins across 3 consecutive contests are brittle and miss streaks spanning more contests.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window ranking row_number difference partitions consecutive series in a single sort pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize gaps-and-islands technique using contest_id - row_number.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_interview_candidates(contests: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    gold = contests["gold_medal"].value_counts()
    golds_3 = set(gold[gold >= 3].index)
    
    all_m = []
    for _, r in contests.iterrows():
        all_m.append((r["contest_id"], r["gold_medal"]))
        all_m.append((r["contest_id"], r["silver_medal"]))
        all_m.append((r["contest_id"], r["bronze_medal"]))
    df_m = pd.DataFrame(all_m, columns=["contest_id", "user_id"]).sort_values(["user_id", "contest_id"])
    
    streak_users = set()
    for uid, grp in df_m.groupby("user_id"):
        cids = sorted(grp["contest_id"].unique())
        streak = 1
        for i in range(1, len(cids)):
            if cids[i] == cids[i - 1] + 1:
                streak += 1
                if streak >= 3:
                    streak_users.add(uid)
            else:
                streak = 1
    candidates = list(golds_3.union(streak_users))
    res = users[users["user_id"].isin(candidates)][["name", "mail"]]
    return res
solutions.approach: Streak counting and set union in pandas
